notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.24_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.24.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.24.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

### Added

- **A storage section in settings.** Ruze never said how much of your disk it
  was using, which on a chat client that keeps every picture anybody has ever
  sent is worth knowing. Settings now shows the total, broken into what it is
  made of — messages, files, the copies unpacked to display them, and
  everything else — with the folder it all lives in.

  Underneath it, a way to clear the copies nothing has opened since a date you
  choose. That is the only part deleted: your messages are shared with everyone
  in a server, so removing one here would remove it for them too, and the file
  store is the only copy this device holds of something you sent. A copy thrown
  away costs nothing — the next time anybody looks at that picture it is
  unpacked again.

- **Send files in a direct message.** A conversation took words and nothing
  else: no attach button, nothing happened when you dropped a file on it, and a
  pasted screenshot went nowhere. It now takes a file the same three ways a
  channel does — the button, a drop, or a paste — and shows what a friend sends
  you, pictures included. The file travels in the half of the conversation your
  device writes, so it is as private as everything else said there.

- **Messages appear the moment you send them, and say when they are still on
  their way.** A pasted screenshot used to go into a silence: the bytes are
  hashed into the blob store before the message exists, so for as long as that
  took there was nothing on screen but a small "Sending…" line at the bottom of
  the window — and if it stalled, the app simply looked broken.

  What you send is now drawn straight away, faded and marked, and becomes the
  real message when it lands. One that fails says so where you can see it, and
  offers to try again rather than losing what you wrote.

  Underneath that, a second mark: a message saved here that no other device has
  synced with you since. On a network with nobody in the middle that is an
  ordinary thing to be — everyone else is asleep — so it reads as a quiet note
  rather than an error, and it clears itself when somebody reconciles with you.

### Changed

- **Updating on Windows is one press.** It used to mean a trip out to the
  browser, a download nobody could find afterwards, a warning about an unknown
  publisher and an installer wizard — six or seven steps to end up where you
  already wanted to be. Ruze now fetches the new version itself, checks it
  against the key this build was compiled with, installs it with a progress bar
  and no questions, and restarts into it.

  It still never happens on its own: the check can look by itself, and the
  installing waits for you to ask. A download that does not match the key is
  refused rather than run, which is the part that makes doing this unattended
  reasonable at all.
